scope: Cloudflare opportunity Worker only. No Next.js redeployment, database reseed, plan upgrade, or test LinkedIn feed post.

cache.invalidation: Generation rotation after successful ingestion, method checks and cleanup; old entries expire automatically.
cache.fallback: D1 on missing/unavailable Redis; 1.5-second command timeouts.
cache.concurrency: Miss coalescing within each Worker isolate; no distributed lock.
cache.privacy: Only existing public catalog payloads; hashed cache identities; secrets in Worker secret bindings.
cache.cost: Usually two Redis GET commands per eligible request, plus SET on miss. No numerical daily D1 savings claimed yet.

import_optimizations: One batch lookup of existing records; compare all normalized content fields.
Unchanged listings receive one grouped last-seen-only update and skip content-column FTS triggers.
Changed, new and reappearing listings still use full upserts.
Cursor rotation, source-failure retention, complete-board removal, expiry and stale rules preserved.
query_optimization: Stats total is summed from grouped category results, removing the separate full eligibility/dedup count query.
deployment_notes: An initial live check exposed unsupported fetch redirect mode error; corrected to manual and reverified all six cache routes on the final deployed Worker.
Live verification performed two empty Buffer snapshots and two nonempty Zapier snapshots, no feed publications.
Worker-only deployment avoids migrations/seeding; existing posting state and both enable flags verified unchanged.
limitations: Public catalog changes may take up to ten minutes to appear if invalidation fails; existing Next data cache may add two minutes.
Redis outages fall back to D1 and can restore high D1 usage.
High-cardinality searches and uncached endpoints still query D1.
No automated future analytics review was scheduled. Compare subsequent UTC daily D1 totals with the prior audit.
